v: Understand why accounts matter
Learn the six basic words

b.v: About 20 minutes. Keep Excel open; every lesson has a small sheet to make.

v: Know if the business really makes a profit
Know who owes you and whom you owe
Get loans, investors and tax filing right
Catch theft and mistakes early
Income (revenue) - money earned from sales or services
Expense - money spent to run the business: rent, salaries, electricity
Asset - what the business owns: cash, stock, equipment, money others owe you
Liability - what the business owes: loans, unpaid supplier bills
Capital (equity) - the owner's money in the business
Profit - income minus expenses

b.v: Assets = Liabilities + Capital. Everything the business owns was paid for either by borrowing or by the owner's money. Every entry you make keeps this balance.
Do this now:|Write 3 examples each of income, expense, asset and liability for a small shop.|Check the equation with simple numbers: cash 50,000 = loan 20,000 + capital 30,000.

v: Understand double entry
Apply the debit and credit rules

b.v: Every transaction touches at least two accounts, and the total debit always equals the total credit. If you buy a chair for Rs 5,000 cash, furniture goes up and cash goes down by the same amount.

v: Assets and expenses: increase = debit, decrease = credit
Liabilities, capital and income: increase = credit, decrease = debit
Owner puts Rs 100,000 in the business: debit Cash, credit Capital
Buy stock for Rs 40,000 cash: debit Stock (Purchases), credit Cash
Sell goods for Rs 15,000 cash: debit Cash, credit Sales
Pay rent Rs 10,000: debit Rent expense, credit Cash
Buy on credit from a supplier: debit Purchases, credit the Supplier (payable)

b.v: Do this now:|Write the debit and credit for 5 transactions of your own business or an imaginary shop.

v: Record every transaction in one sheet
Check that debits equal credits
A: Date
B: Voucher number
C: Account
D: Debit
E: Credit
F: Narration - a short note of what happened

b.v: Step by step:|Type the headings in row 1.|Select the data and press Ctrl + T to make it an Excel table.|Format columns D and E as numbers with a thousands separator.|Under the table, total each column with =SUM().
Put =SUM(D:D)-SUM(E:E) in a cell. It must be 0. If not, a line is missing or one side was typed wrong. Use Data > Data Validation on column C so only names from your account list can be typed.
Do this now:|Make the journal sheet.|Enter 10 transactions from yesterday.|Make sure the difference is 0.

v: See the balance of every account
Build it with one formula

b.v: On a new sheet, list every account in column A: Cash, Bank, Stock, Sales, Purchases, Rent, Salaries, Capital, Loan, each customer and supplier. In column B write its type: Asset, Liability, Capital, Income or Expense.

v: Debit total: =SUMIFS(Journal[Debit], Journal[Account], A2)
Credit total: =SUMIFS(Journal[Credit], Journal[Account], A2)
Balance: debit total minus credit total
Assets and expenses normally have a debit balance (positive)
Liabilities, capital and income normally have a credit balance (negative in this sheet)
A cash balance below zero means a mistake - you cannot spend cash you don't have

b.v: Do this now:|Make the account list.|Add the three SUMIFS columns.|Check that the cash balance matches the cash in your drawer.

v: Prove the books are in balance
Find common mistakes

b.v: A list of every account with its debit or credit balance on one date. The two columns must have the same total.

v: Debit column: =IF(balance>0, balance, 0)
Credit column: =IF(balance<0, -balance, 0)
Total both columns at the bottom and compare
A transaction never entered at all
The right amount in the wrong account (rent posted as salaries)
The same wrong amount on both sides
So also compare cash and bank balances with real cash and bank statements

b.v: Do this now:|Build the trial balance from your ledger.|If the totals differ, find the line that causes it.

day-6.t: Day 6 — Cash book and bank reconciliation

v: Keep a daily cash book
Match your records with the bank statement
Columns: date, details, cash in, cash out, running balance
Running balance: =previous balance + in - out
Count the cash in the drawer every evening and compare
Cheques you issued that the bank has not paid yet
Deposits you made that the bank has not added yet
Bank charges, profit or tax the bank added that you did not record
Mistakes on either side

b.v: Step by step:|Start with the balance in your bank book.|Add issued cheques not yet paid.|Subtract deposits not yet credited.|Adjust for bank charges and profit (and record them in your books).|The result must equal the bank statement balance.
Do this now:|Make a cash book for one week.|Do one reconciliation with last month's bank statement.

day-7.t: Day 7 — Invoices and money customers owe

v: Make a clean invoice template
Track who owes you and for how long
Your business name, address, phone and tax number if you have one
Invoice number and date
Customer name and address
Lines: item, quantity, rate, amount (=quantity * rate)
Subtotal, discount, tax if any, and total
Payment terms: for example 'due within 15 days'

b.v: Keep a sheet with invoice number, customer, date, amount, amount received and balance. Add 'days due' with =TODAY()-date.

v: Group balances into 0-30, 31-60, 61-90 and over 90 days
Call customers before invoices get old
Old balances are hard to collect - follow up politely but regularly

b.v: Do this now:|Make the invoice template and save it as a template file.|Make the receivables sheet with days due.

v: Track what you owe suppliers
Keep a simple stock sheet

b.v: Record every supplier bill with date, amount, amount paid and balance. Pay on time to keep good prices and credit, but check every bill against what you actually received.

v: Columns: item, opening stock, purchased, sold, closing stock
Closing stock: =opening + purchased - sold
Reorder level: highlight the cell with Conditional Formatting when closing stock falls below it
Stock value: closing quantity x cost price

b.v: Count the real stock at least once a month and compare it with the sheet. A difference means breakage, theft or a recording mistake - find which.
Do this now:|Make a stock sheet for 10 items with a reorder level.|Make a supplier balance sheet.

v: Calculate monthly salaries correctly
Keep a clean record for staff
Employee name and CNIC (keep this file private)
Basic salary and allowances
Days present and leave
Overtime
Deductions: advance, absence, any tax or contributions required by law
Net salary = gross salary - deductions
Absence deduction: =basic / days in month * days absent
Gross: =basic + allowances + overtime
Net: =gross - SUM(deductions)
Total of the whole sheet = salary expense for the month
Pay through the bank when you can - it leaves a record
Give each person a payslip
Protect the file with a password; salaries are private

b.v: Do this now:|Make a salary sheet for 3 imaginary staff.|Check the total net salary with a calculator.

day-10.t: Day 10 — Profit and loss and balance sheet

v: Make the two main reports
Set a monthly routine
Sales
minus cost of goods sold (opening stock + purchases - closing stock)
= gross profit
minus expenses (rent, salaries, electricity, delivery)
= net profit for the period
Assets: cash, bank, stock, receivables, equipment
Liabilities: payables, loans
Capital: owner's capital + net profit - drawings
Check: assets = liabilities + capital

b.v: Step by step:|Enter every transaction in the journal weekly.|Reconcile cash and bank.|Count stock.|Print the trial balance, profit and loss and balance sheet.|Compare with last month and write what changed.
For tax returns and audits, work with a qualified accountant. These sheets will make their work faster and cheaper.
